svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.4.2 Masonry Units
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND

g.text: Bed joint: mortar on the inner and
Head joint: mortar on both face
Starting course: full bed of mortar,
Every course of a column: full bed,
Webs next to it: full bed

svg.text: Hollow masonry units are laid with mortar
applied to the head and bed joints of both the
Vertically aligned webs of hollow masonry
units are laid in a full bed of mortar
(a) under the starting course, (b) in all courses
of columns, and (c) where next to cells or
cavities that are to be filled with grout.
Except for head joints left open for weep
holes and ventilation, solid masonry units are
laid with full head and bed joints.
Drawn: some units lifted to show the mortar under them. Unit and core shapes are illustration only.
